REC-FedDyn employs a directly testable relative-error criterion that allows each client to independently control the accuracy of its local subproblem, without a server-side acceptance test. We establish almost-sure iterate convergence for strongly convex and convex problems, almost-sure asymptotic stationarity for nonconvex problems, and communication and parallel gradient-evaluation complexity bounds, all under partial participation and without assuming bounded data heterogeneity. Experiments on image inpainting, fMRI prediction, and neural-network classification with structured regularization demonstrate efficiency and robustness across levels of data heterogeneity and client participation.
tldr: The paper proposes REC-FedDyn, a relative-error composite federated optimization method with one server-side proximal step per communication round.
motivation: Federated optimization with composite regularizers needs communication-efficient methods that tolerate partial client participation and data heterogeneity.
method: REC-FedDyn uses a directly testable relative-error criterion for local subproblem accuracy and performs one server-side proximal evaluation per round, with convergence and complexity analysis.
result: The authors establish almost-sure convergence for convex and strongly convex cases, asymptotic stationarity for nonconvex cases, and communication/gradient complexity bounds under partial participation and unbounded heterogeneity.
conclusion: Experiments on image inpainting, fMRI prediction, and neural-network classification indicate efficiency and robustness, but the work is outside quantum information science.

title: Fixed Detectors, Moving Code: How Well Do Static Security Analyzers Hold Up Over A Decade Of C/c++ Evolution?
authors: Zhengsong Zhang. Haipeng Cai Junhua Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.03742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools are often deployed on the assumption that detectors configured today will remain effective on future code, including previously unknown vulnerabilities. We test this assumption using 20,000 vulnerable and fixed C/C++ cases from 1,116 open-source projects (2016-2025), evaluated with three CodeQL releases, three Infer releases, and one Semgrep configuration. To distinguish temporal effects from shifts in code composition, we compare yearly populations, project- and label-matched year pairs, and within-project trajectories. We investigate the largest within-project declines through repair diffs, detection predicates, alert locations, and execution logs, while accounting for failed, degraded, and costly analyses. Under changed-file case-label scoring, overall F1 ranges from 0.066 to 0.478, but count-based AUROC stays near chance (0.495-0.526). Newer CodeQL releases attain higher F1 alongside nearly parallel rises in recall and false-positive rate, not stronger separation of vulnerable from fixed cases. In project-matched year pairs, CodeQL R2024 has negative mean later-minus-earlier F1 at every source-year gap, whereas Infer v1.1 and v1.3 have positive means throughout. Among selected drops, only 6 of 39 CodeQL and 2 of 620 Infer findings overlap a changed repair line. For Semgrep, 78.96% of cases show parser or timeout diagnostics even though every run reports success. These results suggest that apparent changes in temporal SAST effectiveness can arise from broader alerting, changing analysis coverage, and incidental findings, not solely from losses in vulnerability detection. Evaluations of temporal sustainability should fix detector conditions, control for projects, inspect repair-level evidence, and report failed or degraded analyses.
tldr: A large-scale empirical study of whether static application security testing tools (CodeQL, Infer, Semgrep) remain effective on C/C++ code as it evolves over a decade (2016–2025).
motivation: SAST tools are deployed on the assumption that today's configured detectors will keep catching future vulnerabilities; the authors test this untested assumption about temporal sustainability.
method: They analyze 20,000 vulnerable and fixed C/C++ cases from 1,116 open-source projects using three CodeQL releases, three Infer releases, and one Semgrep configuration, comparing yearly populations, project- and label-matched year pairs, and within-project trajectories, with repair-diff and execution-log inspection.
result: Overall F1 ranges from 0.066 to 0.478 while count-based AUROC stays near chance (0.495–0.526); only 6 of 39 CodeQL and 2 of 620 Infer findings overlap changed repair lines, and 78.96% of Semgrep cases show parser or timeout diagnostics despite reported success.
conclusion: Apparent temporal changes in SAST effectiveness stem largely from broader alerting, shifting analysis coverage, and incidental findings rather than pure loss of detection; evaluations should fix detector conditions, control for projects, inspect repair-level evidence, and report degraded analyses.

title: The Complexity Of Kkt Points Of Quadratic Programs With Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
authors: Argyrios Deligkas, Michail Fasoulakis, Stavros D. Ioannidis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.03945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point of a quadratic polynomial over the unit hypercube is known to be [MATH]-complete, when the coefficients of the polynomial are encoded in binary. We prove that the problem remains [MATH]-complete even when the coefficients are encoded in unary. This is the first problem proven to remain [MATH]-hard when the input is given in unary.
tldr: The paper proves that computing a KKT point of a quadratic polynomial over the unit hypercube remains PLS-complete (or the relevant complexity class) even when coefficients are encoded in unary, giving the first problem proven hard under unary encoding.
motivation: Known hardness results for KKT-point computation assume binary-encoded coefficients; the authors ask whether the problem stays hard under the much weaker unary encoding of the input.
method: Complexity-theoretic reduction showing hardness persists for polynomially-bounded (unary) coefficients.
result: The problem is shown complete for the same complexity class even with unary coefficients, the first such unary-hardness result.
conclusion: Unary encoding does not trivialize KKT-point computation, sharpening the complexity landscape of quadratic programming.

title: Proceedings 23rd International Conference On Quantum Physics And Logic
authors: John van de Wetering, Ognyan Oreshkov, Ana Bel\'en Sainz
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This volume contains the proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Quantum Physics and Logic (QPL 2026), which was held from August 17 to August 21 2026, in Amsterdam, The Netherlands, organized by the University of Amsterdam. QPL is an annual conference that brings together academic and industry researchers working on topics ranging from basic research in the foundations of physics to applications in quantum computing and communication, both for near-term quantum hardware and future large-scale, fault-tolerant devices. The conference places particular emphasis on the application of formal algebraic, logical, compositional, and categorical structures to quantum theory and related areas. Work applying quantum-inspired techniques and structures to other fields such as (classical) computation, linguistics, artificial intelligence, and causality is also welcome.
tldr: This is the proceedings volume of the 23rd International Conference on Quantum Physics and Logic (QPL 2026), covering broad foundational, logical, categorical, and compositional approaches to quantum theory and computation.
motivation: The volume collects contributed papers from a conference spanning quantum foundations, formal methods, categorical structures, and applications to quantum computing and communication.
method: As a proceedings volume, it compiles peer-reviewed conference contributions rather than presenting a single unified research method or result.
result: It provides a snapshot of current work in quantum physics and logic, with emphasis on algebraic, logical, compositional, and categorical structures.
conclusion: The paper is a conference proceedings collection and does not itself advance a specific information-theoretic, thermodynamic, networking, or hybrid-systems research direction.

title: ScrambleMark: Zero-Query Watermark-Agnostic Black-Box Evasion Of Modern Speech Watermarking
authors: Binhao Ma, Weikang Ding, Hanqing Guo, Wenwei Zhao, Xiaowen Li, Leah Ding, Zhuo Lu, Rui Duan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speech watermarking is becoming a key defense for digital copyright and content authentication. Existing attacks treat evasion as a removal problem: they erase the watermark, relying on detector access or on speech data that is hard to collect, such as paired clean-watermarked or clean target speaker speech. Commercial platforms are moving to close off these assumptions. TrustedAudio, for instance, restricts detection to authenticated users and denies meaningful detection feedback to unauthorized parties. Adversaries thus cannot tell whether a sample is watermarked or which watermark it carries, nor reliably remove it without degrading speech quality. In this work, we show that evading a speech watermark does not require erasing it: detection relies on the structural consistency of the embedded pattern, and disrupting this consistency is enough to defeat it. Building on this observation, we identify harmonic structure as an effective attack surface, as perturbing it breaks watermark consistency while preserving perceptual quality. We therefore propose ScrambleMark, a zero-query, watermark-agnostic, black-box attack that evades detection through harmonic scrambling. ScrambleMark combines a deterministic engine for discovering transferable harmonic perturbations with a generative model that learns randomized scrambling patterns, avoiding reliance on fixed attack rules. Across three commercial platforms (Google SynthID, Resemble AI, and TrustedAudio), ScrambleMark is the only attack to both evade detection and keep speech natural, achieving nearly 97% evasion and a 4.2/5 human rating, far above the 1.1 to 1.7 of prior attacks. Beyond evasion, ScrambleMark withstands adaptive recovery designed to reverse it, evidence that structural evasion is hard to mitigate in practice.
tldr: ScrambleMark is a zero-query, black-box adversarial attack that evades speech watermark detection by scrambling harmonic structure rather than removing the watermark itself.
motivation: Commercial speech watermarking platforms increasingly restrict detector access, so adversaries cannot query detectors or obtain clean/watermarked paired data; existing removal-based attacks therefore become impractical, motivating a watermark-agnostic evasion strategy.
method: The authors exploit harmonic structure as an attack surface, combining a deterministic engine that discovers transferable harmonic perturbations with a generative model that learns randomized scrambling patterns, requiring no detector queries or watermark knowledge.
result: Across Google SynthID, Resemble AI, and TrustedAudio, ScrambleMark achieves nearly 97% evasion while retaining a 4.2/5 human naturalness rating, versus 1.1–1.7 for prior attacks, and resists adaptive recovery attempts.
conclusion: Structural disruption of harmonic consistency is a practical and hard-to-mitigate route to speech watermark evasion, exposing robustness gaps in deployed audio watermarking systems.

title: Semidirect Sums Of Tensors And The Matrix Multiplication Exponent
authors: Baitian Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note is an exposition of the recent preprints from OpenAI that establish the bound [MATH] on the matrix multiplication exponent. We argue that the heart of these preprints is a new technique, which we formulate as the untwisting lemma for semidirect sums of tensors. This gives a generally applicable method for analyzing tensors. We also discuss further consequences of this method, as well as the relation between the OpenAI proof and previous work.
tldr: This note expounds recent OpenAI preprints on bounding the matrix multiplication exponent via an untwisting lemma for semidirect sums of tensors.
motivation: The paper aims to clarify and generalize the core tensor technique behind new bounds on the matrix multiplication exponent, making the method more broadly applicable to tensor analysis.
method: It formulates an untwisting lemma for semidirect sums of tensors and uses it to analyze the OpenAI proof strategy, relating it to prior work.
result: The exposition identifies the untwisting lemma as the central new technique and discusses consequences and connections to previous tensor-based approaches.
conclusion: The work is a mathematical exposition in classical algebraic complexity and algorithm design, concerning tensor methods for fast matrix multiplication.

title: VerfGraph: Efficient Zero-Knowledge Verifiable Graph Query Evaluation System
authors: Tianyi Ma, Yuncong Zhang, Yuanzhuo Yu, Boshi Yuan, Shi-Feng Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph databases are often used to manage relationship-rich data, whose graph structure and attributes may be sensitive. In many applications, a database owner or a service provider evaluates queries over a private graph for a client. Because the graph cannot be fully disclosed and independently re-executing the query may be impractical, the client cannot directly verify the returned result. This creates a need for verifiable graph query evaluation that preserves data confidentiality. We present VerfGraph, a zero-knowledge system for verifiable graph query evaluation, which enables a client to verify that the query result was correctly computed over a committed graph data, without revealing private graph records or intermediate query values beyond the public inputs and what is implied by the query result. Building on the expansion-centric model introduced by the state-of-the-art zero-knowledge verifiable graph query evaluation system ZKGraph (ICDE'26), VerfGraph achieves more efficient and expressive zero-knowledge verifiable graph query evaluation by advancing design in two key ways. First, we propose novel operator-proof methods for core expansion and shortest-path operations that reduce costly sorting and comparison checks and eliminate edge canonicalization for bidirectional expansion. Furthermore, we introduce correctness proofs for count and weighted shortest-path operators, broadening the class of graph queries that can be verified. We evaluate VerfGraph using the LDBC Social Network Benchmark. Compared with ZKGraph on complex IC queries, VerfGraph achieves [MATH]-[MATH] speedups in proof generation and reduces peak prover memory by factors of [MATH]-[MATH], while maintaining millisecond-level verification and producing sub-MB proofs.
tldr: VerfGraph is a zero-knowledge system for efficient verifiable graph query evaluation over committed private graph data.
motivation: Graph databases can contain sensitive structure and attributes, so clients need a way to verify query results without requiring full disclosure or independent re-execution of the query.
method: The paper builds on the expansion-centric zero-knowledge verifiable graph query model and introduces new operator proofs for core expansion, shortest paths, count queries, and weighted shortest paths, reducing sorting/comparison overhead and eliminating edge canonicalization for bidirectional expansion.
result: On the LDBC Social Network Benchmark, VerfGraph reports speedups in proof generation and reduced peak prover memory compared with ZKGraph, while maintaining millisecond-level verification and sub-MB proofs.
conclusion: VerfGraph improves the efficiency and expressiveness of zero-knowledge verifiable graph query evaluation, but the work is in classical cryptographic systems and is not aligned with quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: CloakFEM: Agentic Fem Code Generation For Red-Teaming Computational Resource Exhaustion
authors: Simin Chen Li Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite element method (FEM) solvers are foundational to scientific and engineering simulation, yet their susceptibility to remains largely unexplored. An adversary can craft syntactically valid and runnable FEM programs that complete successfully while forcing excessive computational work, enabling computational denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. Finding such inputs is challenging because FEM programs occupy a vast, structured space constrained by numerical, geometric, and constitutive requirements. We introduce CloakFEM, a domain-guided LLM-agent framework for automatically generating runnable adversarial FEM programs that amplify solver computation. CloakFEM combines LLM-guided search with an FEM-specific intermediate representation and a deterministic validity gate that enforces runnable constraints. Across three FEM stacks, 17 problem classes, and 1,068 seeds, CloakFEM discovers adversarial inputs that substantially amplify solver work while remaining valid and solvable. In the most extreme case, solver iterations increase from 43 to 247,367, a \(5{,}752.72\times\) amplification. CloakFEM outperforms five generic black-box baselines and retains an advantage over evolutionary search under a controlled bounded action space. Cross-solver analysis further reveals both problem-intrinsic and solver-specific sources of vulnerability. Our results uncover an underexplored efficiency-attack surface in FEM solvers and show that runnable FEM programs can serve as adversarial inputs.
tldr: CloakFEM is an LLM-agent framework that automatically generates valid but computationally expensive finite-element-method programs to expose resource-exhaustion (denial-of-service) vulnerabilities in FEM solvers.
motivation: The security of numerical simulation software against adversarial inputs that force excessive computation is largely unexplored, and searching the structured space of valid FEM programs for such inputs is difficult.
method: The authors combine LLM-guided search with an FEM-specific intermediate representation and a deterministic validity gate that guarantees syntactically valid, runnable, and solvable programs, evaluated across three FEM stacks, 17 problem classes, and 1,068 seeds against black-box and evolutionary baselines.
result: Adversarial inputs amplify solver work dramatically—up to 5,752.72x more iterations (43 to 247,367)—and cross-solver analysis reveals both problem-intrinsic and solver-specific vulnerabilities.
conclusion: Runnable FEM programs constitute an underexplored adversarial surface for algorithmic-complexity attacks, motivating efficiency-aware hardening of scientific solvers.

title: Entropy-Weighted Soundness For Multi-Answer Birthday Graphs
authors: Alexandru Popa
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The vertices of a Boolean birthday graph are partial assignments on [MATH]-subsets of [MATH] variables. Although a satisfying assignment induces a [MATH]-clique for [MATH], an arbitrary selection of [MATH] vertices may repeat some views and omit others. This makes soundness substantially harder than under uniform view sampling. For bounded-occurrence, constant-gap Boolean ternary CSPs whose constraints each involve three distinct variables (allowing arbitrary Boolean predicates), we prove that the graph's maximum induced [MATH]-vertex density satisfies \[ \rho^*(K)\le 2\exp\!\left(-c\, {n^2\log(en/\ell)}\right) \] for [MATH] and [MATH], with positive constants depending only on the source parameters. The argument refines the biclique counting method by charging the entropy of an adversarially chosen flattening to mutual information and a combinatorial obstruction energy. In the overlapping parameter range it strengthens the explicit soundness exponent previously established for this graph. We also establish an unconditional stability theorem for arbitrary sets [MATH] of exactly [MATH] distinct local assignments, with missing views and multiple answers: [MATH] for every [MATH]. It gives a complementary additive near-clique soundness bound. We do not derive a new fine-grained hardness theorem.
tldr: The paper proves entropy-weighted soundness bounds for multi-answer birthday graphs arising from bounded-occurrence Boolean ternary CSPs.
motivation: Soundness analysis for birthday graphs is harder when selected vertices may repeat views and omit others, unlike uniform view sampling.
method: The argument refines biclique counting by charging the entropy of an adversarially chosen flattening to mutual information plus a combinatorial obstruction energy.
result: It establishes a maximum induced k-vertex density bound and an unconditional stability theorem for sets of exactly t distinct local assignments with missing views and multiple answers.
conclusion: The work strengthens and complements existing soundness exponents for this graph family but does not derive a new fine-grained hardness theorem.

title: A Security Analysis Of Verifiable Credential Verification Pipelines: Attack Surface Arising From Json-ld/rdfc Canonicalization Compared With Sd-jwt Vc And Mdoc
authors: Naohiro Fujie (MIRAI Design Laboratory, ITOCHU Techno-Solutions Corporation, Openid Foundation Japan), Shigeya Suzuki
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluate, at implementation level and under an explicit threat model, the verification pipelines of three Verifiable Credential (VC) formats: SD-JWT VC; the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with the Data Integrity cryptosuite eddsa-rdfc-2022 (W3C VCDM); and mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5). For W3C VCDM we identify and exercise three structural attack surfaces from remote context resolution and RDFC-1.0 canonicalization: denial of service (DoS) via poison graphs, context injection through @context, and server-side request forgery (SSRF) reachable via malicious URLs, all at default settings. A poison graph, whose blank-node references are symmetric enough to force RDFC-1.0 into deep recursion, raises it to 278x the baseline from five blank nodes in 527 bytes, and to 13.5 s from eight. Every experiment ran in four environments sharing runtime and library versions; the multiple moves with the machine (251--424x for one input), not with its speed. Cost tracks that symmetry rather than the node count: an acyclic input with 1,500 blank nodes stays at 462--714x. A call limit separates the two: every attack family aborts at 16 or below, every legitimate credential completes at 1, but a shallow, wide recursion, such as the acyclic control, passes whatever the bound. DoS does not presuppose adversarial input: with production education schemas, canonicalization costs 23--34x a simple credential in one environment, 16--49x across four. Effective mitigations are a static document loader, which removes the retrieval latency and both remote-context surfaces; a context allowlist; and a call limit with a size bound. SD-JWT VC and mdoc need neither canonicalization nor external references, and our verifiers resisted every vector evaluated. These are not format-specific defects but properties of the pipeline and its configuration.
tldr: An implementation-level security analysis of three Verifiable Credential verification pipelines (SD-JWT VC, W3C VCDM with eddsa-rdfc-2022, and mdoc), exposing denial-of-service, context-injection, and SSRF attack surfaces tied to JSON-LD/RDFC canonicalization.
motivation: Verifiable Credential formats differ substantially in whether they require remote context resolution and canonicalization, and the security consequences of these pipeline choices had not been systematically compared under an explicit threat model.
method: The authors built verifiers for all three formats in four controlled environments sharing identical runtime and library versions, then exercised crafted poison graphs, malicious @context injection, and adversarial URLs against default configurations, concluding with mitigation experiments.
result: RDFC-1.0 canonicalization on symmetric blank-node graphs inflates runtime up to 278x from five blank nodes (13.5 s from eight) and 251-424x for a single input across machines, while acyclic inputs with 1,500 blank nodes remain at 462-714x; a call limit of 16 or below aborts all attack families while legitimate credentials complete in one call, and production education schemas alone cost 16-49x baseline.
conclusion: The vulnerabilities stem from pipeline configuration (remote context resolution and canonicalization) rather than format-specific defects; static document loaders, context allowlists, and call limits with size bounds mitigate them, and SD-JWT VC and mdoc, which need neither canonicalization nor external references, resisted all evaluated vectors.

title: Balanced Fair Division And Generalized Kneser Graphs
authors: Amir Jafari Sharareh Alipour
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study indivisible goods allocated to two prescribed nonempty groups whose members have arbitrary monotone valuations. We guarantee balanced envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) for at most five agents and up to two goods (EF2) for at most nine, for any number of goods. Bundle sizes differ by at most one. The EF1 threshold is sharp: every split of six agents can fail. EF2 improves the previous five-agent guarantee. Via the connection of Kyropoulou, Suksompong, and Voudouris, these guarantees follow from chromatic bounds for [MATH], whose vertices are [MATH]-subsets of a [MATH]-set, adjacent when their intersection has size less than [MATH]. We prove its chromatic number is six for [MATH], [MATH], resolving Jafari and Alipour's conjecture, and at least ten for [MATH], [MATH], improving the previous lower bound of six; the known upper bound is fourteen. We show that the standard box-complex [MATH]-index bound yields exactly five and nine for [MATH] and [MATH], respectively. To exceed these bounds, we exploit restrictions on maps induced by colorings: a proper five- or nine-coloring must induce a nonzero homology map, yet local constraints force all generators, supported on pentagon or rook configurations, to map to zero. The ten-color proof compares integral and fractional common centers using a sharp rounding theorem for five subset constraints. A linear-time retraction from the full allocation graph onto balanced layers adds cardinality balance to known nonlinear discrepancy guarantees. For each fixed removal allowance in the guaranteed-existence range, finding a balanced fair allocation or an explicit monotonicity violation from valuation circuits is polynomial-time equivalent to finding a monochromatic edge in a circuit-specified coloring of the corresponding graph. The reverse reduction produces normalized monotone binary valuations using ordinary circuits.
tldr: The paper studies balanced fair division of indivisible goods and proves new chromatic bounds for generalized Kneser graphs.
motivation: It aims to guarantee balanced envy-freeness relaxations (EF1/EF2) for two groups with monotone valuations and to resolve related graph-coloring conjectures.
method: It connects fair-division guarantees to chromatic numbers of generalized Kneser graphs and uses topological/homological arguments, including box-complex index bounds and rounding theorems.
result: It establishes EF1 for up to five agents and EF2 for up to nine agents, proves sharpness of the EF1 threshold, and improves chromatic lower bounds for certain graph parameters.
conclusion: The work advances combinatorial fair division and graph coloring, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mutual-Coupling-Aware Joint Precoding And Antenna Positioning For Movable-Antenna Mu-mimo Systems
authors: Wei Guo, Tianyi Liao, Zixin Wang, Shenghui Song, Jun Zhang, Khaled B. Letaief
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) improve wireless communications by adapting antenna positions to the propagation environment. However, antenna movement also changes the mutual coupling (MC) among elements of the transmit and receive arrays, which affects the performance of MA-enabled systems. In this paper, we investigate MC-aware joint precoding and antenna positioning for a downlink multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system with MAs at both the base station and users. We establish an MC-aware system model by combining field-response propagation with a circuit-based representation of the transmit and receive arrays. Based on this model, we formulate a weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization problem that jointly optimizes multi-stream precoders and antenna positions. The problem is challenging because the precoders and positions are coupled through the propagation channels and position-dependent MC matrices. To address this challenge, we reformulate the problem in the antenna-current domain to to efficiently handle the MC matrices and develop a current-domain weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) framework for alternating optimization. Furthermore, we handle the nonconvex position updates within the framework by using majorization--minimization (MM) and solve the resulting convex subproblems with a dedicated conic alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design improves the WSR over both an MC-aware fixed array and a movable-array design that ignores MC during optimization.
tldr: The paper develops mutual-coupling-aware joint precoding and antenna position optimization for movable-antenna multiuser MIMO downlink systems.
motivation: Antenna movement in movable-antenna systems alters mutual coupling between array elements, and existing designs ignore this effect, degrading performance.
method: An MC-aware system model combining field-response propagation with a circuit-based array representation is built, and a weighted sum-rate maximization is solved via a current-domain WMMSE framework with MM-based position updates and conic ADMM subproblems.
result: Simulations show the proposed design achieves higher weighted sum-rate than MC-aware fixed arrays and movable-array designs that neglect MC during optimization.
conclusion: Accounting for position-dependent mutual coupling is beneficial in movable-antenna MU-MIMO systems, and the current-domain optimization framework handles the resulting coupling efficiently.

title: System-level Performance In Massive Isac Networks
authors: Emanuele Mengoli (MATHNET, IP Paris, INFRES, RMS), Nahuel Soprano-Loto
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a dynamic stochastic geometry framework to model and evaluate large-scale integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. Base stations are distributed according to a homogeneous Poisson point process, while user equipments and sensing objects undergo localised random motion around their serving base station. Full spectrum reuse with a common waveform generates mutual interference that couples the two functionalities. Communication performance is characterised through downlink queues whose service rates are governed by the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) via the Shannon capacity. Sensing performance is captured by a Kalman filter (KF) whose measurement noise covariance depends on the sensing SINR, yielding a non-classical state-dependent filtering problem. We define system-level performance metrics under the Palm distribution of the base station process and prove the consistency of their empirical estimators. We then prove that, for a typical base station, communication and sensing metrics are associated, so that operating regimes favourable to one functionality tend to benefit the other. The proof combines the monotonicity of the queue and filter recursions in the configuration of interferers with the Harris--FKG inequality for Poisson functionals. We also show that the excess association ratio of the two interference levels decays as the inverse of the network density. Simulations based on a ray-tracing channel model corroborate the analysis.
tldr: The paper develops a stochastic-geometry framework for large-scale integrated sensing and communication networks, analyzing coupled communication queues and Kalman-filter sensing performance under shared-spectrum interference.
motivation: ISAC networks require system-level models that capture both communication and sensing performance under mutual interference and user/object mobility.
method: Base stations follow a homogeneous Poisson point process, while users and sensing objects move locally; communication is modeled via SINR-driven downlink queues and sensing via a Kalman filter whose measurement noise depends on sensing SINR, with Palm-distribution metrics and Harris–FKG arguments.
result: The authors prove consistency of empirical estimators and show that communication and sensing metrics are associated for a typical base station, with the excess association ratio decaying inversely with network density; ray-tracing simulations corroborate the analysis.
conclusion: The framework provides system-level performance characterization for massive ISAC networks and identifies operating regimes where communication and sensing benefits align.

title: H\"older Duality And Self-Dual Arc Length On $L^p$ Unit Curves
authors: Jacinto Joaqu\'in Arichabala Concha
abstract: ArXiv:2611.03693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study arc length on the first-quadrant unit curve [MATH], [MATH], when length is measured with respect to an [MATH] norm. Denoting this length by [MATH], we prove the H\"older-duality identity [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH]. The identity is interpreted as a special case of the symmetry of mixed area (equivalently, of the anisotropic perimeter pairing). For the distinguished dual metric [MATH], the length element agrees with the areal angular element: [MATH]. Thus the familiar coincidence between arc length and angular parameter on the Euclidean unit circle is the self-dual case [MATH] of a more general relation between [MATH] geometry and its dual metric. As a consequence, the Euclidean arc length of the [MATH] unit curve admits a dual trigonometric representation.
tldr: The paper proves a Hölder-duality identity relating arc length on first-quadrant L^p unit curves to the dual metric L^q, interpreting it as a special case of symmetry of mixed area (anisotropic perimeter pairing).
motivation: The authors aim to generalize the classical Euclidean coincidence between arc length and angular parameter on the unit circle, showing it arises as the self-dual case p=2 of a broader duality between L^p geometry and its dual metric.
method: Pure convex-geometric and functional-analytic arguments: define arc length with respect to an L^p norm on the unit curve of the first quadrant, then exploit Hölder duality and the symmetry of mixed area / anisotropic perimeter pairing to derive the dual identity.
result: The identity L_p = L_q^* is established with q the Hölder conjugate of p, and for the distinguished dual metric the length element is shown to coincide with the areal angular element, yielding a dual trigonometric representation of the Euclidean arc length of the L^p unit curve.
conclusion: The Euclidean unit-circle relation is recovered as the self-dual special case p=2, providing a unified duality picture between L^p geometry and its dual metric; the work is purely mathematical with no quantum information, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-system content.

title: A Hybrid Tt/qtt Discontinuous Galerkin Method With Fixed-matrix Upwinding For Three-dimensional Transient Multigroup Neutron Transport
authors: Dibyendu Adak, Radoslav Vuchkov, Oleg Korobkin, Ted Sariyski, Boian S. Alexandrov
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a hybrid tensor-train/quantized tensor-train (TT/QTT) upwind discontinuous Galerkin method for three-dimensional transient multigroup neutron transport. The central contribution is a fixed-matrix upwind construction: two spatial DG matrices serve all directions and energy groups, with signed and absolute direction-cosine factors preserving Kronecker structure. For homogeneous materials on uniform Cartesian grids, operator rank bounds are independent of mesh size, group count and direction count at fixed scattering order. We derive a conditional global step-defect bound and enforce group-integrated balance of the compressed system. Crank-Nicolson tests show second-order convergence on a separable manufactured solution whose finest final state occupies 13 kB instead of 35 TB, a compression factor of [MATH]. A modified rank-adaptive basis-update and Galerkin integrator (TT-BUG) advances passive and active bursts with approximately half a billion unknowns. Selected runs are 15-20 times faster than AMEn at comparable verified scalar-flux errors. In the reported anisotropic active-burst configurations, TT-BUG takes 14.3 s on one processor versus 716 s for OpenSn on 24 processors: approximately 50 times less wall time and 1200 times less allocated processor-time cost. This compares reported configurations rather than matched physical errors. OpenSn provides an independent discretization check. The modified TT-BUG source-onset and saturation treatment is tested numerically; its order, convergence and general tolerance-to-error relation remain unproved.
tldr: The authors develop a hybrid tensor-train/quantized tensor-train upwind discontinuous Galerkin solver for three-dimensional transient multigroup neutron transport, achieving extremely large compression factors and large speedups over existing solvers.
motivation: Simulating 3D transient multigroup neutron transport is computationally prohibitive because the state space scales with mesh size, energy groups, and directions; low-rank tensor compression is sought to make such problems tractable.
method: A fixed-matrix upwind DG construction is introduced in which two spatial DG matrices serve all directions and energy groups via signed and absolute direction-cosine factors that preserve Kronecker structure, combined with a rank-adaptive basis-update Galerkin integrator (TT-BUG) and Crank-Nicolson time stepping.
result: Operator ranks are provably mesh-, group-, and direction-independent for homogeneous materials on uniform grids; tests show second-order convergence with final states compressed from 35 TB to 13 kB, bursts of ~0.5 billion unknowns advanced in 14.3 s on one processor versus 716 s for OpenSn on 24 processors.
conclusion: The TT/QTT approach yields order-of-magnitude gains in memory and cost for neutron transport, though the convergence order and tolerance-to-error relation of the modified TT-BUG integrator remain unproved.

title: The Web Doesn't Sit Still: Adversarial Self-Evolving Attacks On Search Agents
authors: Geyuan Wang, Shunyu Liu, Siyuan Liang, Chenyang Lyu, Dacheng Tao
abstract: ArXiv:2611.03754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise for empowering search agents to tackle complex information-seeking tasks. However, since acquiring external information necessitates web search, these agents are highly susceptible to various adversarial attacks (e.g., malicious information injection or stealthy context manipulation). Existing attack strategies inevitably rely on static and human-crafted templates, failing to emulate the dynamic and complex nature of real-world threats. In this paper, we propose an adversarial self-evolution framework that integrates bi-level optimization between the attacker's strategy evolution and the defender's adaptive mitigation, to expose the vulnerabilities of search agents. Specifically, we introduce the Contrastive Rollout Evolutionary Optimization (CREO) method to drive the directional evolution of the attack strategy population via contrastive evolutionary signals. To provide a stable environment for this continuous evolution, we further construct a controlled sandbox and design fine-grained metrics to quantify internal vulnerabilities. Extensive experiments across various multi-hop QA benchmarks and frontier LLMs demonstrate that the proposed framework yields attack efficacy superior to static baselines, underscoring the urgent need to develop more robust defense frameworks.
tldr: The paper proposes an adversarial self-evolution framework (Contrastive Rollout Evolutionary Optimization) that co-evolves attacker strategies against defender mitigations to expose vulnerabilities of LLM-based search agents.
motivation: LLM search agents must query the open web, making them vulnerable to malicious information injection and context manipulation, yet existing attacks rely on static, hand-crafted templates that fail to capture realistic dynamic threats.
method: A bi-level optimization framework couples an evolving population of attack strategies with an adaptive defender inside a controlled sandbox, with contrastive evolutionary signals driving directional strategy improvement and fine-grained metrics quantifying internal vulnerabilities.
result: Experiments on multi-hop QA benchmarks and frontier LLMs show the self-evolving attacks outperform static baselines in attack efficacy.
conclusion: The work highlights the urgent need for more robust defenses for search-augmented LLM agents against dynamic, evolving adversarial threats.

title: Towards Effective Fuzzing Of Edk2 Components
authors: Datta Manikanta Sri Hari Danduri, Connor Everett Glosner, Aravind Machiry
abstract: ArXiv:2611.03854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Securing bootloaders is critical to establishing the trusted computing base of modern systems. TianoCore's edk2, the de facto UEFI-based bootloader, is widely deployed but has recently been shown to contain numerous high-severity vulnerabilities. Existing approaches either focus on post-boot interfaces or rely on heavyweight simulation, limiting their scalability, throughput, and coverage of boot-time components. We present Metis, an automated technique for fuzzing edk2 protocols (i.e., boot-time interfaces) by rehosting them as user-space applications. Our key insight is that effective fuzzing must exercise not only protocol interfaces but also their dependency interactions, which serve as additional input channels. Metis employs a Direct-dependency Component Rehosting (DCR)-based strategy to construct semantically meaningful mocks for dependencies, enabling controlled input injection across all channels. It further leverages a hybrid approach combining static analysis and Large Language Model (LLM)-guided synthesis to generate and refine fuzzing harnesses. We implement Metis on the Host Based Firmware Analyzer (HBFA) framework and evaluate it on 60 drivers covering 162 protocols. Metis achieves 73.1% coverage, approximately 1.7 times higher than FuzzUEr, the state-of-the-art edk2 fuzzing technique, and discovers 137 previously unknown bugs. We have already reported 26 of them, including 12 that are remotely triggerable, and all reported vulnerabilities have been acknowledged by the vendors.
tldr: Metis is an automated fuzzing technique for UEFI edk2 boot-time protocols that rehosts components as user-space applications and uses dependency-aware mocking plus LLM-guided harness synthesis.
motivation: Securing UEFI bootloaders is critical, but existing fuzzing approaches are limited in scalability and coverage of boot-time components.
method: The work rehosts edk2 protocol components in user space, constructs semantically meaningful mocks for dependencies via Direct-dependency Component Rehosting, and combines static analysis with LLM-guided synthesis to generate fuzzing harnesses.
result: Metis achieves 73.1% coverage on 60 drivers covering 162 protocols, about 1.7x higher than FuzzUEr, and discovers 137 previously unknown bugs, 26 reported with 12 remotely triggerable.
conclusion: Dependency-aware rehosting and hybrid harness generation substantially improve fuzzing of UEFI boot-time interfaces, revealing many security vulnerabilities.

title: Algorithmic Non-dimensionalisation Of Polynomial Dynamical Systems With CRNNondim
authors: Martin Wechselberger Georgio Hawi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although non-dimensionalisation is a fundamental step in modelling, it is rarely obvious, especially for large dynamical systems, how to systematically construct optimal non-dimensionalisations. In this work, we develop a general mathematical framework for non-dimensionalising polynomial ODEs by interpreting them as chemical reaction networks (CRNs) and characterise the space of admissible scalings. Within this viewpoint, admissible scalings of time and species are encoded by Laurent monomials, and we derive exact formulae for the minimal number of multiplicative dimensionless parameters required by the reaction-channel coefficients and by the full initial value problem, together with characterisations of the scale assignments that attain structural lower bounds. These counts are expressed in terms of structural properties of the underlying CRN, and we show that the full initial value problem requires no more parameters than the corresponding Buckingham count. These results lead to constructive algorithms which we analyse rigorously and implement in the open-source Python package CRNNondim, available at [URL] . Given a polynomial system or CRN, CRNNondim determines species and time scalings that bring variables as close to unity as possible while minimising the number of free parameters, and among the admissible scalings it chooses free parameters that result in the corresponding dimensionless system being sparse and simple. We apply CRNNondim to numerous well-known biological and biochemical models, yielding simpler dimensionless systems with fewer free parameters, and interpreting the parameters that govern their dynamics.
tldr: The paper develops a mathematical framework and open-source Python package (CRNNondim) for systematically non-dimensionalising polynomial ODE systems by interpreting them as chemical reaction networks.
motivation: Non-dimensionalisation is a fundamental but often ad hoc step in modelling, and there is no systematic way to construct optimal dimensionless forms for large dynamical systems.
method: Polynomial ODEs are recast as chemical reaction networks, admissible time and species scalings are encoded as Laurent monomials, and exact formulae are derived for the minimal number of dimensionless parameters needed by reaction channels and by the full initial value problem, yielding constructive algorithms implemented in CRNNondim.
result: The framework yields structural lower bounds on parameter counts tied to CRN structure, shows the full IVP never requires more parameters than the Buckingham count, and produces sparser, simpler dimensionless systems with fewer free parameters on numerous biological and biochemical models.
conclusion: CRNNondim provides an algorithmic, structure-aware approach to non-dimensionalisation that simplifies large polynomial models and clarifies the parameters governing their dynamics.

title: Infinite-Horizon Stochastic Recursive Differential Games With Jumps: Nonautonomous Coefficients And Nonzero Terminal Values
authors: Sheng Luo, Qingmeng Wei, Yaxin Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate a class of decoupled infinite-horizon forward--backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) with time-dependent coefficients and jumps. Under suitable time-integrability conditions on the coefficient growth and stochastic Lipschitz moduli, we establish an [MATH] theory ([MATH]) for these systems, including well-posedness, moment estimates, conditional stability, and tail estimates, without imposing dissipativity of the forward dynamics or monotonicity of the backward generator in its value variable. In particular, the forward state converges in [MATH] and almost surely to a limiting random variable [MATH], while the backward solution converges to the generally nonzero terminal value [MATH]. Within this framework, we study infinite-horizon two-player zero-sum stochastic recursive differential games. We prove that the lower and upper value functions are deterministic and establish the dynamic programming principle (DPP) using backward stochastic semigroups and nonanticipative strategies. Both value functions converge locally uniformly to [MATH] as the initial time tends to infinity and are characterized as viscosity solutions of the corresponding non-autonomous, nonlocal Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman--Isaacs (HJBI) equations. Under an additional integrable Lyapunov-barrier condition, we establish a comparison principle for continuous viscosity subsolutions and supersolutions of uniform linear growth, provided that at least one is uniformly Lipschitz in space. This yields uniqueness for both HJBI equations in the linear-growth class. Finally, we establish a weaker, contact-wise Isaacs criterion ensuring that the lower and upper value functions coincide and hence that the game has a value.
tldr: The paper develops an L^p theory for infinite-horizon forward–backward stochastic differential equations with jumps and time-dependent coefficients, and applies it to solve two-player zero-sum stochastic recursive differential games via viscosity solutions of nonlocal HJBI equations.
motivation: Infinite-horizon FBSDEs with jumps and nonautonomous coefficients are needed to characterize stochastic differential games whose backward components converge to nonzero terminal values, a setting not covered by existing well-posedness theory that typically assumes dissipativity or monotonicity.
method: The authors establish well-posedness, moment estimates, conditional stability and tail estimates for decoupled FBSDEs under time-integrability and stochastic Lipschitz conditions, then derive dynamic programming principles with backward stochastic semigroups and nonanticipative strategies, and prove comparison/uniqueness for viscosity solutions of HJBI equations under an integrable Lyapunov-barrier condition.
result: Both value functions are shown to be deterministic, to converge locally uniformly as the initial time tends to infinity, and to be the unique viscosity solutions of the corresponding non-autonomous nonlocal HJBI equations in the linear-growth class; a contact-wise Isaacs criterion guarantees the game has a value.
conclusion: The work provides a self-contained probabilistic framework for infinite-horizon stochastic recursive games with jumps, extending FBSDE and viscosity-solution theory beyond dissipative or monotone regimes, but it is purely a stochastic-analysis contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Complexity Of ReLU Network Synthesis From A Parameter Multiset
authors: Dimitrios Myrisiotis
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We ask how hard it is to build a neural network when its parameter values are given in advance. An instance supplies a multiset of rational numbers, a target behavior, and a bound on the number of neurons, output included. The question is whether one can choose the graph of a ReLU network within the bound, and place the numbers on its edges and biases so that it meets the target. This separates the numbers from the architecture; permutation training instead fixes the hidden units and only rearranges the output weights. Matching two labeled examples exactly is already [MATH]-complete; we ask what changes when the target must hold on every input or on average. Agreeing with a Boolean circuit on every Boolean input is [MATH]-complete, already for four neurons. Agreeing with a given ReLU network on every real input lies in [MATH] for every fixed neuron bound and is [MATH]-complete for three neurons. Approximating a ReLU network on the unit cube within absolute error one everywhere is [MATH]-complete, even with no hidden neurons and all numbers equal and positive. Deciding whether some network has expected squared loss at most a threshold is [MATH]-complete for uniform Boolean inputs. For uniform inputs on the unit cube and for standard Gaussian inputs with a positive threshold, the same holds for two neurons when a positive risk gap, given in binary and possibly exponentially small, separates yes from no instances. Without a gap, the cube version is complete for guessing a polynomial-length string, then comparing a sum of exponentially many rationals with a threshold, all computable in polynomial time from the input and the guess. Since the graph is chosen too, the reductions must rule out every other network built from the same numbers.
tldr: The paper studies the computational complexity of synthesizing ReLU neural networks when the multiset of parameter values is fixed in advance and only the graph/architecture may be chosen.
motivation: Motivated by 'permutation training' and by the general question of separating a network's numerical parameters from its architecture, the author asks how hard it is to assign given numbers to edges and biases of some graph so that a target behavior is realized.
method: Complexity-theoretic reductions are constructed for several variants of the problem: exact agreement with Boolean circuits, agreement with a given ReLU network on all reals, uniform approximation on the unit cube, and expected squared loss thresholds under Boolean, uniform-cube, and Gaussian input distributions.
result: Matching two labeled examples exactly is already complete for a high complexity class, agreement with a Boolean circuit is complete already for four neurons, real-input agreement is complete for three neurons, and approximation on the unit cube is complete with no hidden neurons; gap and no-gap versions of the loss-threshold problem are also classified.
conclusion: Network synthesis from a fixed parameter multiset is computationally intractable in a strong, class-complete sense, and the reductions must exclude every alternative network built from the same numbers because the graph itself is chosen.

title: Polynomial Vass MDPs
authors: Michal Ajdarow
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Markov decision process over vector addition system with states (VASS MDP) is a finite state model combining non-deterministic and probabilistic behavior, augmented with non-negative integer counters that can be incremented or decremented during each state transition. VASS MDPs can serve as abstractions of probabilistic programs, offering many decidable properties. In this paper, we develop techniques for analyzing the polynomiality of asymptotic estimates for VASS MDPs. That is, for every initial configuration of size \(n\), we consider the number of transitions needed to reach a configuration with some counter negative. We show that for any VASS MDP, either for all \(\epsilon>0 \) and all sufficiently large \(n\) the number of transitions is at least \(2^{n^{{2}-\epsilon}} \) with probability at least \(1-\epsilon \), or for any superpolynomial function \(f \), all \(\epsilon>0 \) and all sufficiently large \(n\) the number of transitions is upper bounded by \(f(n) \) with probability at least \(1-\epsilon \). Furthermore, if the VASS MDP is DAG-like then we can replace \(f(n)\) with \(n^{k+\epsilon} \), where \(k=2\cdot 3^{w\cdot d+|T|} \) and \(w,d\) and \(T \) are the number of MECs, counters and transitions of the VASS MDP, respectively. It is decidable in polynomial time which case holds.
tldr: This paper characterizes when termination-time asymptotics for vector addition system with states (VASS) Markov decision processes grow polynomially versus exponentially, with a polynomial-time decision procedure.
motivation: VASS MDPs abstract probabilistic programs with unbounded integer counters, and knowing whether reachability of a counter-negative configuration takes polynomial or exponential time in the initial size would give strong complexity guarantees for such abstractions.
method: The author develops analytical techniques on the structure of maximal end components (MECs) of VASS MDPs, proving a dichotomy: either termination is at least 2^{n^{2-epsilon}} with high probability, or it is bounded by any superpolynomial function; a DAG-like restriction sharpens the bound to n^{k+epsilon}.
result: A clean exponential-versus-polynomial dichotomy is established for all VASS MDPs, and for DAG-like VASS MDPs an explicit polynomial degree k = 2·3^{w·d+|T|} is derived; the case distinction is decidable in polynomial time.
conclusion: The work provides foundational complexity-theoretic insight into probabilistic counter systems, but it lies entirely within classical verification and algorithmic model theory with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: When Debate Amplifies Risk: Social-Bias Vulnerabilities In Multi-Agent Safety Deliberation
authors: Qinghua Mao, Xi Lin, Yuxin Qi, Zihao Xu, Jinze Gu, Yuliang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented Web applications increasingly employ multi-agent debate (MAD) to aggregate conflicting, noisy, and heterogeneous information, yet deliberation is fundamentally a social process susceptible to interpersonal dynamics. When retrieved Web sources contain latent hazards alongside safe factual content, social biases such as conformity pressure and authority deference can override evidence-grounded safety boundaries. In this work, we investigate whether the social structure of deliberation can paradoxically amplify latent Web safety risks. We introduce SafeConflict-Bias, a controlled counterfactual diagnostic protocol spanning six core Web risk categories, which holds queries and retrieved evidence strictly invariant while isolating conversational majority sway, authority cues, and confidence asymmetry. Empirical evaluation across diverse proprietary and open-source backbones reveals that while isolated models reliably reject unsafe guidance, standard MAD catastrophically capitulates to social pressure---surging unsafe adoption from 0.0\% up to 100.0\% and systematically silencing safe minority evidence. To resolve this systemic fragility without retraining or debate regeneration, we propose RiskTrace-Debias, an inference-time auditing framework uniting evidence-first precommitment, social-metadata masking, and consistency-gated arbitration. RiskTrace-Debias suppresses worst-case unsafe adoption to [MATH] across all architectures without inducing over-refusal, while generating verifiable provenance traces to audit interpersonal manipulation in Web deliberation.
tldr: The paper shows that multi-agent debate over retrieved web content can amplify latent safety risks through social biases like conformity and authority deference, and proposes an inference-time debiasing/auditing framework to mitigate this.
motivation: Multi-agent debate is widely used to aggregate noisy web-retrieved information in LLM applications, but deliberation is a social process whose interpersonal dynamics (conformity pressure, authority cues, confidence asymmetry) may override evidence-grounded safety boundaries.
method: The authors introduce SafeConflict-Bias, a controlled counterfactual diagnostic protocol across six web risk categories that holds queries and evidence invariant while isolating majority sway, authority cues, and confidence asymmetry; they then propose RiskTrace-Debias, an inference-time framework combining evidence-first precommitment, social-metadata masking, and consistency-gated arbitration.
result: Across proprietary and open-source backbones, standard multi-agent debate raises unsafe adoption from 0.0% up to 100.0% and silences safe minority evidence, while RiskTrace-Debias suppresses worst-case unsafe adoption without inducing over-refusal and emits verifiable provenance traces.
conclusion: Social structure in LLM deliberation can paradoxically amplify safety risks from retrieved web content, motivating inference-time auditing and debiasing mechanisms that require neither retraining nor debate regeneration.

title: Bilateral Protection For Private LoRA Inference With Intel Tdx
authors: Xiaodong Li, Mingyuan Ma, Dongbo Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cloud services using private low-rank adaptation (LoRA) must protect client inputs and outputs alongside owners' proprietary parameters and execute the approved adaptation. We design and implement a system for bilateral protection of private LoRA inference using Intel Trust Domain Extensions (TDX), connecting approved application identity to actual artifact consumption and adapter activation. The client and LoRA owner independently verify remote attestation, application identity, and binding to the actual Transport Layer Security (TLS) public key before releasing inputs and the weight-decryption key. A fixed read-only image and verified-byte consumption connect approved identities to inference objects, with all inference inside a trust domain. Experiments on real TDX hardware reject controlled application and boot-parameter modifications before secret release. Across 400 fixed dialogues, protected and native CPU inference in the same trust domain produce identical token sequences for all 400 pairs. Across 12 independent trust-domain boots, the steady-state service-to-native time ratio is 1.0094, with a 95% interval of [1.0064, 1.0126]. The system connects bilateral secret release, approved model use, and task-capability preservation, providing verifiable implementation and cost evidence for confidential inference with a public base and private adapter.
tldr: A systems-security design that uses Intel TDX trusted execution to give bilateral protection of client data and LoRA owner weights during private LoRA inference in the cloud.
motivation: Cloud-hosted private LoRA inference must simultaneously hide the input of the client and the proprietary adapter weights of the owner, while still enforcing which approved application and adapter may be used.
method: The authors build a TDX-based system that binds approved application identity to actual artifact consumption, requires both parties to independently verify remote attestation and TLS key binding before releasing secrets, and runs all inference inside a trust domain with a fixed read-only image.
result: On real TDX hardware, unauthorized application or boot-parameter changes were rejected before secret release; protected inference matched native CPU token sequences on all 400 dialogues, and steady-state overhead was about 1.0094x native (95% CI [1.0064, 1.0126]) over 12 boots.
conclusion: The work provides verifiable implementation and cost evidence for confidential split-model inference with a public base model and private adapter, but it is a hardware-security/systems contribution with no quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networking content.

title: Labtune: Treating Lab Organization And Information Sharing As Experimental Variables In LLM-Agent Discovery
authors: Goran Mitevski
abstract: ArXiv:2611.03935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: De-siloing can create groupthink; silos can prevent knowledge sharing and reduce research efficiency. The same tension appears in research systems built with large language model (LLM) agents, yet their organization is usually fixed by design. I propose treating laboratory structure and information sharing as experimental variables. I introduce Labtune, an open framework for bounded research workflows with user-selected laboratory organization, communication policy, model configuration and budget. Users can choose among six editable designs, from multidisciplinary silos and transdisciplinary teams to co-leaders, hub-and-spoke structures, flat co-labs and a single scientist. Information sharing can independently vary from none to high detail, with an optional channel for conditional abstractions called wisdom. Sharing is enforced by the controller at phase barriers rather than through unrestricted agent chat, while delegation does not create additional budget or permissions. Development evidence is separated from protected confirmation, and an optional multi-lab layer allows laboratories with different structures to exchange filtered information. Labtune is an idea and system-description paper, not a benchmark result. Its contribution is to make laboratory organization and information sharing configurable and measurable under matched budgets. I do not claim that one design or level of sharing is best; the aim is to create a concrete experimental space in which those differences can be tested.
tldr: Labtune is a framework that makes laboratory organization structure and information-sharing policy configurable experimental variables for LLM-agent-based research workflows.
motivation: Research systems built from LLM agents typically have fixed organizational structure, even though the trade-off between siloed efficiency and de-siloed groupthink is known to matter in human labs.
method: The authors introduce an open framework with six editable lab designs (multidisciplinary silos, transdisciplinary teams, co-leaders, hub-and-spoke, flat co-labs, single scientist) and independently varying information-sharing levels, enforced by a controller at phase barriers, with matched budgets and separated development/confirmation evidence.
result: No benchmark results are reported; the paper is a system-description and idea paper outlining the experimental space and its optional multi-lab information-exchange layer.
conclusion: The contribution is to make lab organization and information sharing measurable and configurable under matched budgets, without claiming any particular design is best.

title: Multi-modal Laplace-based Sampling
authors: Maxime Eg\'ea, Hanyue Gu, Daniel Rudolf, Bj\"orn Sprungk
abstract: ArXiv:2611.03773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the multi-modal Laplace approximation, given by a weighted Gaussian mixture centred at the local minima of the negative log-density, for sampling from probability measures that concentrate around finitely many modes as an inverse-temperature parameter [MATH] grows. Such distributions occur in Bayesian inference in the small noise or large data regime. We derive explicit, non-asymptotic bounds on the Hellinger distance between the multi-modal Laplace approximation and the concentrating posterior. The bound decays like [MATH] with [MATH] and the constants depend only polynomially on the dimension [MATH]. Moreover, we analyse the Laplace mixture as a proposal distribution for self-normalised importance sampling and independent Metropolis--Hastings (IMH) targeting concentration multimodal distributions. We derive asymptotic results, as [MATH], on the effective sample size in case of importance sampling as well as on the average acceptance probability, lag-one autocorrelation, and spectral gap in case of IMH. Numerical experiments illustrate and verify our theoretical findings.
tldr: The paper develops multi-modal Laplace approximations for concentrated multimodal distributions and analyzes their use in importance sampling and independent Metropolis-Hastings.
motivation: Sampling from multimodal posterior distributions in small-noise or large-data regimes is difficult, and Gaussian mixture approximations around local modes can provide tractable proposals.
method: The authors derive non-asymptotic Hellinger-distance bounds for the multi-modal Laplace approximation and analyze its performance as a proposal in self-normalized importance sampling and independent Metropolis-Hastings.
result: They obtain dimension-polynomial constants and asymptotic results for effective sample size, acceptance probability, autocorrelation, and spectral gap as the inverse-temperature parameter grows.
conclusion: The multi-modal Laplace mixture is a theoretically justified and practically useful proposal for concentrated multimodal distributions, supported by numerical experiments.

title: LoRA-Patch: Defending Against Backdoored LoRA Adapters Via Directional Steering
authors: Shengyan Huo, Peihai Jiang, Xixiang Lyu, Yige Li
abstract: ArXiv:2611.03752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Third-party LoRA adapters introduce serious backdoor risks: malicious adapters can maintain normal task performance while embedding hidden, trigger-activated behaviors, making them difficult to detect through standard utility evaluations. Existing removal-based defenses typically sanitize backdoored models by updating, pruning, distilling, or mixing model parameters. However, these approaches are misaligned with adapter-based deployment, where the trusted base model is expected to remain frozen. In this work, we propose LoRA-Patch, a lightweight backdoor defense tailored to LoRA adapters. Our key insight is that backdoor injection distorts the directional geometry of a poisoned adapter relative to its trusted base model. Building on this insight, LoRA-Patch suppresses trigger-activated behaviors by realigning adapter directions through layer-wise steering, without modifying the base model weights. Extensive experiments across five backdoor attacks and three models show that LoRA-Patch effectively mitigates trigger-activated backdoors, outperforming existing baselines while preserving benign task performance. Moreover, LoRA-Patch is computationally efficient, constructing patches within 20 seconds across all evaluated models and adapters. Our code is publicly available at [URL].
tldr: LoRA-Patch is a lightweight defense that removes backdoor behavior from third-party LoRA adapters by realigning their directional geometry relative to a frozen trusted base model.
motivation: Third-party LoRA adapters can contain hidden trigger-activated backdoors while preserving normal task performance, and existing removal-based defenses are poorly suited to adapter-based deployment because they modify the base model.
method: The authors observe that backdoor injection distorts the directional geometry of a poisoned adapter and propose layer-wise directional steering to suppress trigger-activated behaviors without changing base model weights.
result: Experiments across five backdoor attacks and three models show that LoRA-Patch mitigates trigger-activated backdoors, outperforms baselines, preserves benign performance, and constructs patches within 20 seconds.
conclusion: LoRA-Patch provides an efficient adapter-specific backdoor defense compatible with frozen-base-model deployment, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Aero-VPA: Few-Step Flow-Matching Control Over Non-Reconstructive Jepa Latents For Agile Flight On Edge Hardware
authors: Yeonseok Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generalize across tasks, but their autoregressive decoders need sequential forward passes in proportion to the action horizon, each bounded below on embedded aerial platforms by streaming billions of parameters from memory. We present Aero-VPA, a lightweight Vision-Predictor-Action architecture for 3D navigation on edge hardware. A compact RGB-D Vision Transformer and a five-head ensemble predictor, trained without pixel reconstruction, forecast the next latent state; a Conditional Flow Matching solver generates a velocity and yaw-rate chunk in two Euler steps, so each decision takes five sequential network evaluations; and the ensemble dispersion drives an uncertainty fallback. Version 1 specified the architecture, deployment and protocol without results. This version reports the first closed-loop evaluation: PX4 software-in-the-loop simulation of quadrotor missions in procedurally generated forests. Behaviour cloning failed on all 60 missions despite open-loop errors of 0.02-0.04 m/s: the policy copies its last command, a copycat form of causal confusion. DAgger with a privileged, safety-gated supervisor gave the first successes but plateaued at 11.1-21.1% across six checkpoints. A map-free runtime shield with a 15 s depth memory, barrier constraints, a cap on motion outside the 73-degree field of view and backoff along the flown path raised the first DAgger policy's success on 180 paired missions from 21.1% to 52.2% (95% CI [45.0, 59.4]; exact McNemar p = 1.2 x 10^-10) and cut its crashes from 72.2% to 22.2%, while timeouts rose from 2.8% to 23.3%. All six checkpoints gained 30.0-34.4 percentage points, at mean speeds of 1.16-1.36 m/s. The code ([URL] the trained policy (72.6 MB, [URL] and the full benchmark dataset are public.
tldr: Aero-VPA is a lightweight Vision-Predictor-Action architecture that uses a non-reconstructive JEPA-style latent predictor and a two-step conditional flow-matching solver to enable agile quadrotor flight on edge hardware.
motivation: Autoregressive VLA models require sequential forward passes proportional to the action horizon, making them impractical on embedded aerial platforms with limited memory bandwidth; a compact few-step generative policy is needed.
method: An RGB-D Vision Transformer plus a five-head ensemble predictor trained without pixel reconstruction forecasts the next latent state, a conditional flow-matching solver emits velocity and yaw-rate chunks in two Euler steps, and ensemble dispersion triggers an uncertainty fallback; closed-loop evaluation uses PX4 software-in-the-loop forest missions with behaviour cloning, DAgger, and a map-free runtime safety shield.
result: Behaviour cloning failed on all 60 missions due to copycat causal confusion, DAgger plateaued at 11.1-21.1% success, and the runtime shield raised one policy from 21.1% to 52.2% success while cutting crashes from 72.2% to 22.2%, with all six checkpoints gaining 30-34 percentage points.
conclusion: Few-step flow-matching over non-reconstructive latent predictors combined with a runtime safety shield yields a viable, publicly released edge-deployable agile flight policy, though success rates remain moderate.

title: The Devil Is In The Context: Nine Dimensions Of Prompt Injection Attacks
authors: Jiamin Chang, Kristina Nikoli\'c, Rishi Sharma, Giovanni Cherubin, Vasilios Mavroudis, Jose Sanchez Vicarte, Arnav Garg, Hammond Pearce, Andrew Paverd, Ahmed Salem
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection is usually discussed and evaluated as a single, homogeneous type of attack. However, vulnerabilities reported in real-world systems show that prompt injections vary widely. Moreover, the same instruction can be a prompt injection in one context and a legitimate request in another, depending on the user's intent and the system's policies. Ignoring this variation leaves gaps in how defenses are evaluated, and can give a false sense of security against real-world attacks. We identify nine dimensions along which prompt injection attacks differ. Together, they form a taxonomy that describes the injected instruction itself, its relation to the user's task, and how it manifests in the target system. Each dimension affects which defenses can detect or prevent an attack. We first use the taxonomy to characterize six real-world prompt injection vulnerabilities, showing how much these attacks differ. We then apply it to nine prompt injection benchmarks and find that most cover only a small region of this space. Combining benchmarks helps, but 13% of pairwise category combinations remain untested, mostly among the less commonly represented categories. Finally, we show that the taxonomy supports automated annotation of benchmarks and targeted generation of new test cases to fill these gaps. The taxonomy is also useful beyond benchmarks. Defense authors can use it to state which types of prompt injection they evaluated against, and system operators can use it to identify which attacks apply to their system and choose defenses to match.
tldr: The paper proposes a nine-dimension taxonomy of prompt injection attacks against LLM-based systems and uses it to characterize real-world vulnerabilities, audit nine existing benchmarks, and guide targeted generation of new test cases.
motivation: Prompt injection is typically treated as a single homogeneous attack class, but real-world vulnerabilities vary widely and context determines whether an instruction is malicious, leading to gaps in defense evaluation and a false sense of coverage.
method: The authors identify nine dimensions describing the injected instruction, its relation to the user's task, and its manifestation in the target system; they apply the taxonomy to six real-world vulnerabilities, nine benchmarks, and automated annotation and test-case generation.
result: Real-world attacks differ substantially across the taxonomy, most benchmarks cover only a small region of the attack space, and even combined benchmarks leave about 13% of pairwise category combinations untested.
conclusion: The taxonomy supports benchmark auditing, automated annotation, targeted test generation, and clearer communication by defense authors and system operators about which attack types are covered.

title: Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment Of Fossil- And Bio-Based Membrane Manufacturing
authors: Elizabeth Aigaje-Espinosa, Christina Carbrello, Rui Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.04117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The transition towards sustainable membrane manufacturing is challenged by its reliance on fossil-based polymers, organic solvents, and generation of large volumes of contaminated water. We combined process simulation, life cycle assessment, and Monte Carlo simulation to identify hotspots in the manufacturing of ultrafiltration hollow-fiber membranes for pharmaceutical applications and evaluate strategies to mitigate impact and reduce waste generation. Process models informed by industry input compared fossil- and bio-based membranes on a cradle-to-gate basis per square meter of membrane produced. Key environmental hotspots include polymer and bore solution preparation, driven by the contribution of polymer and solvent, accounting for 30-80% of total impacts across the categories investigated, and wastewater dilution, driven by the environmental burden of solvent-contaminated wastewater management. Under the modeled conditions, although polymer substitution can reduce environmental burdens, cellulose-based membranes show higher impacts than polysulfone membranes in at least 85% of simulations within each impact category, due to chemical-intensive cellulose modification and regeneration. In contrast, solvent recycling can mitigate solvent- and wastewater-related burdens when combined with reduced water demand, yielding climate change benefits at water demands below approximately 36 L per m2 under the modeled recovery configuration and highlighting its potential to reduce the environmental footprint of membrane manufacturing.
tldr: A cradle-to-gate life cycle sustainability assessment comparing fossil-based and bio-based ultrafiltration hollow-fiber membranes for pharmaceutical use, combining process simulation, LCA, and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis.
motivation: Membrane manufacturing relies on fossil-derived polymers, organic solvents, and generates large volumes of contaminated wastewater, so identifying environmental hotspots and evaluating mitigation strategies is needed for a sustainable transition.
